rows.question: Can you cancel my car insurance after I've had it for six months?
rows.answer:
**Yes, but only for a few specific reasons.** Once your policy has been in effect for more than 60 days, as yours has at six months, the policy limits when we can cancel it.

**The allowed reasons:** After a policy has been in effect for 60 days, we will cancel only for nonpayment of premium, or if your driver's license or that of any driver who lives with you or customarily uses your covered auto has been suspended or revoked, or if the policy was obtained through material misrepresentation. In plain terms, those reasons are:
- You didn't pay your premium.
- Your license, or the license of a driver who lives with you or regularly uses your car, was suspended or revoked.
- The policy was obtained through material misrepresentation, meaning important information on the application was false.

**How much notice you'd get:** We may cancel this policy by mailing notice to the named insured. Notice for nonpayment is at least 10 days; for any other reason, at least 20 days.

This explains what the policy wording says. Whether a cancellation applies in a particular situation would depend on the specific facts.

rows.question: My tires got damaged by a pothole. Will collision pay?
rows.answer:
**Probably not, if only the tires were damaged.** The policy excludes tire damage from road hazards when the damage is limited to the tires.

**Why the tires alone likely aren't covered**
The physical damage exclusions say the company will not pay for damage due and confined to wear and tear, freezing, mechanical or electrical breakdown or failure, or road damage to tires. A pothole that damages only your tires fits "road damage to tires."

**If the damage went beyond the tires**
The exclusion applies only to damage *confined* to the tires. If the pothole also damaged other parts, such as the wheels, rims, or suspension, that damage could be looked at under Collision Coverage. Two things matter:

- **Whether you have Collision Coverage.** The policy pays for collision loss only if the Declarations indicate that Collision Coverage is provided. Check your Declarations page.
- **Whether the event counts as a collision.** "Collision" means the upset of your covered auto or a non-owned auto or their impact with another vehicle or object. The policy doesn't specifically say whether hitting a pothole counts. Your claim adjuster would decide that.

**How payment would work if covered**
- The company pays minus any applicable deductible shown in the Declarations.
- Payment is limited to the lesser of the actual cash value of the stolen or damaged property, or the amount necessary to repair or replace the property with other property of like kind and quality.

I can't make a final coverage decision. If parts other than the tires were damaged, it's worth reporting the claim and describing everything that was damaged.

rows.question: How long after a hailstorm can I still file a claim?
rows.answer:
**In Texas, you generally have one year after the date of the hailstorm to report the claim.** Under the Texas Windstorm and Hail Deductible Endorsement, a claim for windstorm or hail damage must be reported to us within one year after the date of the windstorm or hail event, unless good cause exists for later reporting. This applies if that Texas endorsement is part of your policy, which your policy documents or Declarations page will show.

**Don't wait longer than you need to.** Your base homeowners policy also asks you to give prompt notice to us or our agent after a loss. Reporting soon after the storm is the safest approach, even though the endorsement allows up to one year.

**Other deadlines to know about:**
- **Inspection:** We will inspect the damage within 15 days after receiving notice of the claim, unless a catastrophe has been declared, in which case the inspection period may be extended by 15 days.
- **Proof of loss:** You must send to us, within 60 days after our request, your signed, sworn proof of loss.
- **Protecting your home:** In the meantime, you're expected to protect the property from further damage and make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect it.
- **Replacement cost:** For building damage, you may make a claim on an actual cash value basis and then make a claim for any additional replacement cost within 180 days after the loss. For hail damage to your roof, how it's paid depends on the roof's age. Loss to roof surfacing caused by windstorm or hail is settled at actual cash value, not replacement cost, if the roof surfacing is more than 15 years old at the time of loss.

This explains what the policy language says. Whether a particular claim is covered depends on the facts of the loss and your specific policy.

rows.question: The insured wants to invoke appraisal. What's my deadline to respond?
rows.answer:
**You have two deadlines: acknowledge the appraisal request in writing within 5 business days, and name the company appraiser within 20 days after receiving the insured's written request.** If the insured invokes appraisal, acknowledge the request in writing within 5 business days and name the company appraiser within the 20-day window in HO-3 Section 6.5.

**Policy basis (HO-3 §6.5):**
- **When appraisal applies:** Appraisal is available only for a dispute over the amount of loss. If you and we fail to agree on the amount of loss, either may demand an appraisal of the loss.
- **When the 20 days starts:** The clock starts when you receive a written request. Each party will choose a competent and impartial appraiser within 20 days after receiving a written request from the other. If the insured has only asked verbally, the 20-day window under §6.5 hasn't technically started. The 5-business-day acknowledgment in CHG §4.3 is triggered when the insured invokes appraisal.
- **What happens next:** The two appraisers will choose an umpire. A decision agreed to by any two will set the amount of loss.
- **Costs:** Each party pays its own appraiser and shares equally the expense of the umpire.

No state endorsement applies here, so these are the base HO-3 and internal guideline timelines.
